text:
Matthew Schaefer is the face of the Islanders now, and Eyes On Isles said so in a headline this week. The second-year defenseman keeps collecting teenage records, and his pair with Logan Stanley gets 56% of the expected goals in the most minutes of any Islanders pair. Stefen Rosner of NHL.com noted Friday that Schaefer "has been human these last five or so games," and that the rest of the group has to step up more than it has.

That is the honest read on the whole team. New York is 12-8-5, but it gets only 46.6% of the expected goals, and it has allowed nearly 16 fewer goals than the shots against it deserve, the best goaltending cushion in our tables. Our numbers say the Islanders have about five more points than their chances earned. Semyon Varlamov was very good again Friday against Winnipeg, by Rosner's account.

Pete DeBoer has spent the week shuffling. He reunited Mathew Barzal with Bo Horvat, then tried Barzal between Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund. Holmstrom has been on a seven-game point streak, and the Horvat, Holmstrom and Kyle Palmieri line has 58% of the expected goals. The week also had a lovely moment: Casey Cizikas was honored for his 1,000th NHL game.

Our numbers give New York a 38% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: the shot share, because a team leaning this hard on its goalies needs the skaters to close the gap before the saves stop coming.
